fixes.why: The summary says only 'some churches' keep the seventh day and then refers to 'the traditions named on this page', yet reading 1 names no tradition. The seventh-day bodies that hold this reading as a body (Seventh-day Adventist, Seventh Day Baptist) are absent, so the reading looks thinner than its holders make it, and a Baptist reader cannot see that a free-church body is among its holders. held_by can stay empty, since the allowed list has no seventh-day tradition, but the summary can name them.
fixes.fix: Replace the last two sentences of the reading 1 summary with: 'Seventh-day Adventist, Seventh Day Baptist and other seventh-day churches keep the seventh day, Saturday, as their day of rest and worship. None of the traditions in the other two readings holds this reading as a body.'

fixes.where: reading 3 (the Lord's Day as the Christian Sabbath), summary
fixes.why: 'many of them holding the second reading instead' is a claim about the majority of a tradition that the card cannot support and that a Pentecostal reader would not recognise. Pentecostal and Charismatic congregations differ, and the sentence should say only that.
fixes.fix: Replace 'Pentecostal and Charismatic congregations differ widely, many of them holding the second reading instead.' with 'Pentecostal and Charismatic congregations differ widely, some holding this reading and others the second.'

fixes.where: reading 3 (the Lord's Day as the Christian Sabbath), summary
fixes.why: 'Reformed confessions state this most fully' ranks one tradition's statement above the others, and the word 'most' weighs in the way the brief's verdict list warns against. The point is only that the Reformed confessions state the reading at length.
fixes.fix: Replace 'Reformed confessions state this most fully;' with 'Reformed confessions state this at length;'.

fixes.why: The agreed block quotes Exodus 31:16 but not the sign language that Exodus 31:17 gives: the Sabbath is a sign between the LORD and Israel for ever. That sign is the Torah's own account of how the command stands in relation to Israel, and a rabbi reader would expect it beside the covenant clause. The count limit is 4 to 8 passages, and the agreed block already has 8, so the owner must decide whether to add a ninth or swap one out.
fixes.fix: Add to the agreed passages a ninth entry, {"ref": "Exodus 31:17", "quote": "It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever;"}, and add to the agreed summary after 'a permanent covenant for the generations to come' the words 'and a sign between the LORD and Israel for ever'. If the count is to stay at 8, the owner must choose which passage yields.

fixes.why: 'as a commandment given to Israel' is accurate as far as it goes but leaves out the sign that the Torah gives with it, and the sentence on Jewish keeping is a fact from outside the Berean text. A rabbi reader would prefer the Torah's own terms and the usual times of observance stated plainly.
fixes.fix: Replace the Shabbat note's second sentence with: 'Jewish communities keep it from sundown on Friday to nightfall on Saturday, as a sign and commandment given to Israel; this page sets out how Christians read what the Law, the Prophets and the New Testament say of it.'

fixes.why: The reason given for putting the seventh-day reading first is 'the practice of the first believers', a contested historical claim that a Catholic or Orthodox reader would dispute. The reviewers read _why, and the order is visible to every reader, so the stated basis should be one the card can defend, namely when each reading is first set down in writing by its holders.
fixes.fix: In _why, replace 'by when each reading was articulated, as I read the history. First the seventh day kept, the practice of the first believers and the one the church's earliest texts presuppose, which some churches have kept ever since.' with 'by the date each reading is first set down in writing by its holders. The seventh day kept comes first, then the reading that the Sabbath is fulfilled in Christ, then the Lord's Day reading.'

summary: The card's quotes are all exact (32 of 32 against the Berean server), the four passage sets are balanced at eight each, and no verdict word was found outside the quotes. It ships once the seventh-day reading names its bodies in its summary, the wording of two readings is tightened, and Exodus 31:17 is added to the agreed block.
